note: URL Redirect stores each rule as a url_redirect config entity (url_redirect.url_redirect.<id>) with keys path, redirect_path, redirect_for (Role|User), roles, users, negate, message (Yes|No), status (0|1). A kernel REQUEST subscriber (priority 33) issues a 301 TrustedRedirectResponse when the current user's role/identity matches an enabled rule for the current path (supports <front>, * wildcards, external http(s) targets). Medium cases read back a seeded rule's destination/target role; hard cases build a new rule and verify the config entity's fields on the live site. configure route = entity.url_redirect.collection (/admin/config/system/url_redirect). Depends on core path; provides 3 admin permissions.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal url_redirect module, how is a single redirect rule stored, and what fields decide the source path, the destination, and who the redirect applies to?
evals.expected_output: Each rule is a url_redirect config entity (url_redirect.url_redirect.<id>). Key fields: path (source), redirect_path (destination), redirect_for (Role or User) with roles/users, plus negate, message (Yes/No) and status (enabled/disabled).

evals.prompt: How does url_redirect actually perform the redirect for a matching visitor, at what point in the request, and what HTTP status code does it send? Does it support wildcards or external URLs?
evals.expected_output: A KernelEvents::REQUEST subscriber at priority 33 (before the router) matches the path against enabled rules (exact, <front>, or * wildcards via path.matcher), checks the current user's roles/identity (negate inverts), and returns a 301 TrustedRedirectResponse. External http(s):// targets are used as-is; <front>/empty go to the front page; other internal targets are base-URL prefixed. It also runs on 403 EXCEPTION events.

evals.prompt: This site has a url_redirect rule (machine name urlr_known) that redirects the path /urlr-known-src. Inspect the live configuration and state the destination path (redirect_path) that this rule sends visitors to.
evals.expected_output: The urlr_known rule redirects /urlr-known-src to /urlr-known-dest (redirect_path in url_redirect.url_redirect.urlr_known; readable via drush config:get).

evals.prompt: A url_redirect rule with machine name urlr_role is configured on this site as a Role-based redirect. Inspect the live configuration and state which role it applies to.
evals.expected_output: urlr_role has redirect_for = Role and roles = [anonymous], so it applies to the anonymous role (from url_redirect.url_redirect.urlr_role).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a url_redirect rule with machine name urlr_task that redirects the internal path /urlr-task-src to /urlr-task-dest for the authenticated role, and make sure it is enabled. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A url_redirect.url_redirect.urlr_task config entity with path=/urlr-task-src, redirect_path=/urlr-task-dest, redirect_for=Role, roles containing authenticated, and status=1.

evals.prompt: Create a url_redirect rule with machine name urlr_ext that redirects the internal path /urlr-ext-src to the EXTERNAL URL https://example.com for the authenticated role, enabled, and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A url_redirect.url_redirect.urlr_ext config entity with path=/urlr-ext-src, redirect_path=https://example.com (external, used as-is by TrustedRedirectResponse), redirect_for=Role with authenticated, status=1.
